# Grouped row MEAN and COUNT

The 23 complete reports in `row_reductions.tsv` were independently enumerated before native replay and compared with actual Python reference execution while candidate native imports were forbidden. Twenty successes retain exact CSV bytes; three scope failures retain complete source observations, the authored aggregate path, expression and driver-scope reason. Candidate observations never write expected truth. Existing expected fixtures and the assisted inventory remain unchanged.

Explicit source typing fixes numeric inputs independently of output conversion. MEAN cases cover integer and float inputs, skipped missing values, all-missing and empty groups, signed zero, ordered forward/reverse floating accumulation, integer output conversion and multiple groups. Float bits are enumerated separately from CSV spelling; the CSV profile renders integral floats without `.0`, including `-0`. COUNT cases cover records versus present values, raw text and Unicode, all-missing and empty groups, typed numeric fields and multiple groups. Invalid relation and unqualified-operand cases stop after ingestion, retain the source table and reject saving.

The shared core compiler lowers admitted grouped row reductions to existing immutable engine expressions: ordered numeric SUM/MEAN, record counts and present-value counts. It retains authored expression/source identities and driver scope. No new reducer executes in a binding or adapter. Both installed hosts replay complete reports twice with fresh/cached capture accounting, exact successful saves and failed-save gates.

This qualifies only direct grouped driver fields and COUNT of the driver's qualified record star. Other reducers, nested arithmetic, reduction filters/keys, row-output dependencies, intermediate row drivers, warning severity and the public frontend remain separate work. The original row-conversion and column-check suites continue to protect their existing phases and declared checkpoints.
